parsed.rationale: This is not normal: the rhythm is regular and the QRS is narrow, but there is right axis deviation (small r and deep S in lead I, tall R in III), a dominant R wave in V1 with T-wave inversion in V1–V3, and persistent S waves in V5–V6, which fits right ventricular hypertrophy with strain. None of the 12 diagnoses fits that pattern, so I chose other. There is no significant ST elevation, so it does not meet STEMI criteria.
